messages.subject: Unbalanced grid.arrange widths
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to use grid.arrange to plot five meteorological variables in one single figure. I could use facet_wrap, but it wouldn't allow me to create separate y-axis labels, hence I'll stick to grid.arrange.

Based on previous discussions here on the list I managed to create the plot. However, I noticed that when the numbers on the y-axis on a graph are longer that the others, the figures are not completely aligned.

Here is the reproducible code. Please note how the precipitation and net radiation plots have different widths in comparison to the others:

# Load packages to
require(reshape2)  # melt data.frame
require(ggplot2)   # create plots
require(scales)    # deal with dates on x-axes
require(gridExtra) # align final plots in single column
require(plyr)      # subset data while plotting
require(RCurl)     # download data

# Read data
link<-getURL("https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/27700634/data.csv")
weather <- read.csv(textConnection(link),header=F, sep=',', stringsAsFactors = FALSE, as.is=TRUE)
names(weather) <- c('Year', 'Julian',  'Hour',  'Temperature', 'Net Radiation', 'Precipitation', 'Humidity', 'Wind')

# Combine the first three columns into a character vector
date_info <- with(weather, paste(Year, Julian, Hour))

# Parse that character vector
weather$date <- strptime(date_info, "%Y %j %H")

DF1 <- data.frame(weather, Day = as.Date(format(weather$date))) 

new <- aggregate(cbind(Humidity, Temperature, Wind, Net.Radiation) ~ Day, DF1, mean)
tmp <- aggregate(cbind(Precipitation) ~ Day, DF1, sum)
new$Precipitation <- tmp$Precipitation

# Melt data by date
data <- melt(new, id='Day')

#################################################################
# Alternate version, using "gridExtra" grid arrangement instead of facet 
#################################################################
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=Day, y=value, ymin = 0)) + 
  scale_x_date(breaks = '1 month', labels = date_format('%b-%y'),
               limits = as.Date(c('2012-01-01','2013-01-01'))) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.margin = unit(0,'lines'), axis.title.x = element_blank()) 

#################################################################
# Create Plot 1: Precipitation
#################################################################
prec <- p + geom_bar(subset = .(variable == 'Precipitation'), stat='identity') +
  labs(x = NA, y = 'Precipitation (mm)') +
  theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())

#################################################################
# Create Plot 2: Humidity
#################################################################
humi <- p + geom_line(subset = .(variable == 'Humidity'), linetype='solid') +
  labs(x = NA, y = 'Relative humidity (%)') +
  theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())

#################################################################
# Create Plot 3: Temperature
#################################################################
temp <- p + geom_line(subset = .(variable == 'Temperature'), linetype='solid') +
  ylab('Air temperature (°C)')

#################################################################
# Create Plot 4: Net radiation
#################################################################
nrad <- p + geom_point(subset = .(variable == 'Net.Radiation')) +
  ylab (expression(paste("Net radiation (","W.",day^-1,")", sep="")))

#################################################################
# Create Plot 5: Wind
#################################################################
wind <- p + geom_line(subset = .(variable == 'Wind'), linetype='solid') +
  ylab (expression(paste("Wind speed (","m.",s^-1,")", sep="")))

# Assemble figure
grid.arrange(prec, humi, temp, nrad, wind, ncol = 1)


Is there any way to fix that?

Many thanks in advance,
Thiago.

messages.subject: Re: Unbalanced grid.arrange widths
parts:
Try this,

# http://stackoverflow.com/a/21503904/471093
align_plots = function(...){
  pl <- list(...)
  ## test that only passing plots
  stopifnot(do.call(all, lapply(pl, inherits, "gg")))
  gl <- lapply(pl, ggplotGrob)
  bind2 <- function(x,y)
    gtable:::rbind_gtable(x,y,"first") # bug with pmax
  
  combined <- Reduce(bind2, gl[-1], gl[[1]])
  
  wl <- lapply(gl, "[[", "widths") # now do the pmax manually
  combined$widths <- do.call(grid::unit.pmax, wl)
  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::grid.draw(combined)
}

align_plots(prec, humi, temp, nrad, wind)


HTH,

b.

parts:
This might help you. Try this:

 

library(grid)

pp1 <- ggplotGrob(prec)

pp2 <- ggplotGrob(humi)

pp3 <- ggplotGrob(temp)

pp4 <- ggplotGrob(nrad)

pp5 <- ggplotGrob(wind)

 

grid.draw(rbind(pp1,pp2,pp3,pp4,pp5, size="first"))

 

Janesh
